attributes.name: repeat_finding
attributes.description: Indicates whether this finding is a recurrence of a previously identified finding at the same site for the same category. Repeat findings are a key risk indicator in risk-based monitoring (RBM) and may trigger escalation or CAPA initiation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; EMA Reflection Paper on RBM

attributes.name: resolution_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the finding in its resolution lifecycle. open: finding identified, awaiting site response. in_progress: site has acknowledged and is working on resolution. resolved: corrective action completed and verified by CRA.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS; MasterControl CAPA

attributes.name: resolved_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the finding was resolved and the corrective action was verified as complete by the CRA. Null if the finding has not yet been resolved. Used to calculate resolution cycle time for KPI reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: root_cause
attributes.description: The identified root cause of the finding as determined through investigation by the site or CRA. Documented as part of the CAPA or corrective action process.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl CAPA; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; ISO 14155

attributes.name: sdv_completed
attributes.description: Indicates whether the required Source Data Verification (SDV) for this finding has been completed by the CRA. Applicable only when sdv_required is True.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: sdv_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether Source Data Verification (SDV) is required as part of the corrective action for this finding. True when the finding involves data discrepancies that require verification against original source documents.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.3; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: severity
attributes.description: Risk-based severity classification of the finding indicating its potential impact on subject safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance. Critical: immediate risk to subject safety or data integrity requiring urgent action.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline; ISO 14155

attributes.name: site_response
attributes.description: Narrative response provided by the site (Principal Investigator or Clinical Research Coordinator) acknowledging the finding and describing the corrective actions taken or planned. Captured in the CTMS and included in the monitoring visit report.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18.6; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: site_response_date
attributes.description: The date on which the site provided its formal response to the finding. Used to measure site responsiveness and compliance with response timelines defined in the monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: subject_number
attributes.description: Subject identifier. PII. Implements SDTM DM.SUBJID subject identifier concept.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM USUBJID; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: subject_safety_impact
attributes.description: Indicates whether this finding has a direct or potential impact on the safety or welfare of study subjects. True findings require immediate escalation per GCP requirements and may trigger safety reporting obligations.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 4.11; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; ICH E2A; ISO 14155

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time at which this finding record was most recently modified in the CTMS. Supports audit trail requirements and change tracking under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: visit_type
attributes.description: Type of monitoring visit during which this finding was identified. site_initiation: pre-enrollment site setup visit. interim_monitoring: routine on-site or remote monitoring visit. close_out: end-of-study visit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.50; Oracle Siebel CTMS

products.name: monitoring_action_item
products.description: Formal action item raised as a result of a monitoring finding, protocol deviation, or escalation trigger. Tracks action description, responsible party (site staff, CRA, or sponsor), due date, priority level, current status (open, in-progress, overdue
products.reference: Action Item / Follow-Up Item (GCP, ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18.4)

attributes.name: monitoring_action_item_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the action item record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key generated by the lakehouse ingestion pipeline from the source system
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice

attributes.name: central_monitoring_alert_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to monitoring.central_monitoring_alert. Business justification: A monitoring action item can be raised as a direct result of a central monitoring alert (e.g., KRI breach requiring site-level follow-up action).
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: compliance_capa_id
attributes.description: Reference to the formal CAPA record in MasterControl associated with this action item, when the finding severity warrants a full CAPA workflow. Null for minor action items not escalated to CAPA.
attributes.references: MasterControl; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; ISO 14155

attributes.name: parent_action_item_monitoring_action_item_id
attributes.description: Self-referencing identifier linking this action item to a parent action item when it was created as a sub-task or follow-up from a prior finding. Supports hierarchical action item tracking and recurrence analysis.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: primary_monitoring_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the responsible party (site staff, CRA, or sponsor representative) accountable for resolving this action item. Drives automated escalation workflows in the source system for overdue items.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Workday HCM

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_id
attributes.description: Reference to the protocol deviation record that triggered this action item, where applicable. Supports traceability between deviations and corrective actions per GCP requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.5; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: site_monitoring_visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the monitoring visit (initiation, interim, or close-out) during which this action item was identified or formally raised. Null if the action item originated outside a scheduled visit (e.g., remote review or escalation trigger).
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study (protocol) under which this action item was raised. Links the action item to the governing study protocol for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); CDISC SDTM IG; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site at which the action item was identified. Enables site-level performance tracking and regulatory inspection readiness reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 4; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.62

attributes.name: tertiary_monitoring_closure_confirmed_by_user_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the CRA, monitor, or sponsor representative who reviewed the closure evidence and formally confirmed the action item as resolved. Supports electronic signature audit trail per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: trial_subject_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to subject.trial_subject. Business justification: Subject-specific action items (missing ICF, SDV discrepancy for a specific subject, unreported AE) are a standard CTMS operational concept.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: action_item_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-visible reference number for the action item as assigned by the source system (e.g., AI-STUDY001-00042). Used in monitoring visit reports, CAPA correspondence, and regulatory inspection documentation.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: action_type
attributes.description: Classifies whether the action item represents a corrective action (addressing an existing finding), preventive action (mitigating future risk), observation (noted but not requiring immediate action), recommendation, or escalation.
attributes.references: MasterControl; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.1; FDA 21 CFR Part 820.100; ISO 14155

attributes.name: monitoring_action_item_category
attributes.description: Business classification of the action item by the type of finding or compliance gap it addresses. Drives routing logic, escalation thresholds, and regulatory reporting groupings in the source system
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline; CDISC

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the action item was formally closed following verification of corrective action completion and evidence review. Null for open or in-progress items.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: closure_evidence_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the evidence provided to confirm resolution of the action item (e.g., updated SOP reference, re-training record, corrected eCRF entry, SDV confirmation). Required for GCP-compliant closure documentation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; ALCOA+ Principles; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: closure_evidence_document_ref
attributes.description: Reference identifier or URL to the supporting document stored in Veeva Vault eTMF that substantiates the closure of this action item (e.g., training certificate, corrected source document scan, updated SOP version).
attributes.references: Veeva Vault eTMF; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this action item record was first created in the source system Provides the audit trail creation event per 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements and ALCOA+ contemporaneous documentation standards.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: ctms_record_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Record ID
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the source system for this action item. Preserved in the Silver Layer to enable bidirectional traceability between the lakehouse and the operational system of record.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8

tag_set.value: Clinical Trial Management System (CTMS) Record ID

attributes.name: data_integrity_impact
attributes.description: Indicates whether the finding underlying this action item compromises the integrity of clinical trial data (e.g., eCRF entries, source data, audit trail). When True, may require data query issuance in Medidata Rave EDC and notification to data management.
attributes.references: ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Data Integrity Guidance 2018; MHRA Data Integrity Guidance

attributes.name: days_overdue
attributes.description: Number of calendar days the action item has been open past its due date (or extended due date if applicable). Populated by the source system automated workflow; zero for on-time or not-yet-due items.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance 2013

attributes.name: monitoring_action_item_description
attributes.description: Full narrative description of the monitoring finding, protocol deviation, or compliance gap that necessitated this action item. Includes observed facts, regulatory reference, and expected corrective action per GCP documentation standards (ALCOA+).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; ALCOA+ Principles; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the responsible party must complete and close the action item. Used by the source system automated escalation workflows to flag overdue items and notify CRA supervisors and sponsor representatives.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the action item was formally escalated. Null if is_escalated is False. Used to measure escalation response time and regulatory inspection readiness.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: escalation_reason
attributes.description: Narrative explanation of why the action item was escalated, including the triggering condition (e.g., overdue beyond threshold, critical safety implication, repeated non-compliance). Required when is_escalated is True.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: extended_due_date
attributes.description: Revised due date granted after a formal extension request and approval. Null if no extension has been granted. Tracks due date changes for audit trail and SLA compliance reporting.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: gcp_reference
attributes.description: GCP reference. Implements ICH E6(R2) Good Clinical Practice guideline reference.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline; ISO 14155; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: is_escalated
attributes.description: Indicates whether this action item has been formally escalated to a higher authority (e.g., sponsor medical monitor, regulatory affairs, DSMB) due to non-resolution, critical priority, or subject safety risk.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: last_updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this action item record in the source system Used for incremental data pipeline processing and audit trail completeness per 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) Section 8; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: monitoring_visit_type
attributes.description: Type of monitoring visit during which the action item was identified. Denormalized from the monitoring visit record for reporting efficiency. Supports analysis of finding patterns by visit type (e.g., higher deviation rates at initiation visits).
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance 2013

attributes.name: priority
attributes.description: Priority level assigned to the action item indicating urgency and potential impact on subject safety, data integrity, or regulatory compliance. Critical items trigger immediate escalation workflows in the source system
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: raised_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which the action item was formally raised and entered into the source system Serves as the principal business event date for SLA calculation, aging analysis, and regulatory inspection timelines.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: recurrence_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this action item represents a recurring finding previously identified at the same site or study. Recurring findings may trigger escalation to a formal CAPA workflow and are tracked for site performance risk scoring.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance 2013; MasterControl CAPA

attributes.name: regulatory_impact
attributes.description: Assessment of the potential regulatory impact of the finding underlying this action item. Drives prioritization for regulatory submission readiness, inspection preparation, and escalation to regulatory affairs.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EMA GCP Guideline; ICH E6(R2); EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: response_date
attributes.description: Date on which the site formally submitted their response to the action item. Used to measure site responsiveness KPIs and to determine whether the response was received within the required timeframe.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: response_text
attributes.description: Formal written response provided by the site (PI or CRC) acknowledging the action item and describing the planned or completed corrective actions. Captured in the source system as part of the action item resolution workflow.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 4.1; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: responsible_party_role
attributes.description: Functional role category of the party accountable for resolving the action item. Distinguishes between site staff (PI, CRC), CRA, sponsor, or functional team (data management, safety). Used for workload distribution and escalation routing.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: source_type
attributes.description: Identifies the originating activity or process that generated this action item (e.g., on-site monitoring visit, remote monitoring review, SDV finding, protocol deviation, safety signal, audit). Supports risk-based monitoring (RBM) analytics.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance 2013; EMA Reflection Paper on RBM

attributes.name: monitoring_action_item_status
attributes.description: Current workflow state of the action item lifecycle in the source system Overdue status is set automatically when the due date passes without closure. Closed status requires documented evidence of resolution.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: subject_safety_impact
attributes.description: Subject safety impact flag. Implements ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.18.4 subject safety concept.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 4.11; ICH E2A; FDA 21 CFR Part 312.32; EMA GCP Guideline

attributes.name: title
attributes.description: Short, descriptive title summarizing the action item finding or required corrective action. Used as the primary display label in CTMS dashboards, monitoring visit reports, and escalation notifications.
attributes.references: Oracle Siebel CTMS; ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18

attributes.name: verification_method
attributes.description: Method used by the CRA or monitor to verify that the corrective action was implemented and the action item can be closed (e.g., SDV, document review, on-site visit, remote review). Supports GCP audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; Oracle Siebel CTMS

products.name: risk_indicator
products.description: Centralized monitoring risk indicator (also known as Key Risk Indicator or KRI) defined within the RBM monitoring plan. Captures indicator name, category (enrollment, data quality, safety, protocol compliance, IP accountability), calculation method
products.reference: Key Risk Indicator (KRI) / Risk-Based Monitoring (TransCelerate RBM, ICH E6(R2))

attributes.name: risk_indicator_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for the centralized monitoring risk indicator (Key Risk Indicator / KRI) record within the Risk-Based Monitoring (RBM) framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance (2013); EMA Reflection Paper on Risk-Based Quality Management

attributes.name: compliance_obligation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to compliance.obligation. Business justification: KRIs are defined to monitor compliance with specific regulatory obligations. Linking risk_indicator to obligation enables obligation coverage reporting — confirming each regulatory
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: kri_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.program_kri. Business justification: Study/site-level KRIs (risk_indicator) are operationally mapped to program-level KRIs (program_kri) for aggregation into program_kri_readings.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: lab_panel_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_panel. Business justification: Risk-Based Monitoring (RBM) plans define KRIs per lab panel (e.g., safety panel completion rate, critical value rate by panel).
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: monitoring_plan_id
attributes.description: Reference to the RBM monitoring plan document that defines this KRI, linking the indicator to its governing plan version and associated thresholds.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; Veeva Vault eTMF

attributes.name: risk_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to program.program_risk. Business justification: Site/study-level risk indicators that breach thresholds are escalated to the program risk register.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: service_level_agreement_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to agreement.service_level_agreement. Business justification: KRIs are frequently mapped 1:1 to SLA thresholds in CRO contracts (e.g., query rate, data entry lag, SDV completion).
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: site_monitoring_visit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the monitoring visit (on-site or remote) during which this KRI was reviewed or triggered a visit activity. Links centralized monitoring findings to on-site monitoring actions.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS Visit entity

attributes.name: statistical_endpoint_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.statistical_endpoint. Business justification: KRIs in RBM are defined per statistical endpoint (e.g., missing primary endpoint data rate, primary endpoint query rate).
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this Key Risk Indicator (KRI) is defined. Links the KRI to its parent protocol and RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC SDTM IG; Oracle Siebel CTMS Study entity

attributes.name: study_site_id
attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site for which the KRI value is computed. A single KRI definition may produce one computed record per site, enabling site-level risk scoring within the RBM framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; Oracle Siebel CTMS Site entity

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current risk alert status of the KRI for the site, derived by comparing the computed value against amber and red thresholds. Drives site risk scoring and monitoring intensity decisions in the RBM framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: amber_threshold
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value at which the KRI triggers an amber (warning) alert, indicating elevated risk requiring heightened monitoring attention. Defined in the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: Formal description or formula specifying how the KRI value is computed (e.g., 'Number of screen failures / Number of subjects screened × 100'). Ensures reproducibility and auditability of centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) outputs.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; CDISC ADaM; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: capa_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) must be initiated in response to the KRI breach. Drives workflow integration with MasterControl CAPA tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; MasterControl CAPA; ISO 9001

tag_set.value: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag

attributes.name: risk_indicator_category
attributes.description: Business category classifying the domain of risk the KRI monitors. Supports stratified risk reporting across enrollment, data quality, safety, protocol compliance, and Investigational Product (IP) accountability domains.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: computation_date
attributes.description: Calendar date on which the KRI value was most recently computed for the site. Used to assess data currency and trigger recomputation schedules in the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: computation_frequency
attributes.description: Scheduled frequency at which the KRI is recomputed for each site (e.g., weekly for enrollment KRIs, monthly for data quality KRIs). Defined in the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: computation_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time at which the KRI value was computed, including timezone offset. Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: computed_value
attributes.description: Current computed numeric value of the KRI for the associated site, derived from the source system data as of the last computation run. This is the principal quantitative fact of the risk indicator record.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: consecutive_breach_count
attributes.description: Number of consecutive computation cycles during which the KRI has remained at or above the amber or red threshold. Used to trigger escalation workflows and CAPA initiation per the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; MasterControl CAPA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this KRI record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Operational system of record from which the KRI input data is extracted for computation (e.g., Medidata Rave EDC for data quality KRIs, the source system for safety KRIs, the source system for enrollment KRIs).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: denominator_value
attributes.description: Raw denominator component of the KRI computation (e.g., total subjects screened, total expected data points, total SAEs reported). Stored alongside the numerator to enable independent verification of the computed value.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: effective_from
attributes.description: Date from which this KRI definition became active and applicable to the study and site. Supports versioning of KRI definitions when monitoring plan amendments are issued.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: effective_until
attributes.description: Date on which this KRI definition was superseded or retired. Null for currently active KRI definitions. Supports historical analysis and monitoring plan amendment tracking.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the current KRI alert status and breach history require formal escalation to the sponsor, Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), or senior management per the RBM escalation procedure.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: indicator_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of what the KRI measures, its business rationale, and how it supports risk detection within the RBM framework.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: indicator_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the KRI as defined in the RBM monitoring plan (e.g., 'Screen Failure Rate', 'Missing Data Rate', 'SAE Reporting Timeliness'). Used in dashboards, monitoring visit reports, and sponsor communications.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance

attributes.name: indicator_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the KRI definition within the monitoring plan. Active KRIs are computed and monitored; draft KRIs are under review; retired KRIs are no longer in use.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; MasterControl Document Control; Veeva Vault

attributes.name: indicator_type
attributes.description: Risk indicator type. Implements ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.0 risk-based quality management KRI/QTL concept.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; TransCelerate RBM Framework; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: is_centralized_monitoring
attributes.description: Indicates whether this KRI is part of the Centralized Statistical Monitoring (CSM) program, as opposed to a site-level operational indicator. Supports differentiation of CSM KRIs from operational monitoring metrics.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for CRA or data manager annotations regarding the KRI computation, alert status, or remediation context. Supports monitoring visit report narrative and sponsor communication.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: numerator_value
attributes.description: Raw numerator component of the KRI computation (e.g., number of screen failures, number of missing data points, number of overdue SAE reports). Stored to support audit and recomputation validation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ Principles; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: prior_computed_value
attributes.description: KRI computed value from the immediately preceding computation cycle for the same site. Enables trend analysis and detection of rapid deterioration or improvement in site risk profile.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: red_threshold
attributes.description: Numeric threshold value at which the KRI triggers a red (critical) alert, indicating a significant risk requiring immediate escalation and corrective action per the RBM monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; TransCelerate RBM Framework

attributes.name: reference_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the data window used to compute the KRI value. Together with reference_period_start, defines the exact temporal scope of the KRI computation for reproducibility and audit.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Risk-Based Monitoring Guidance; ALCOA+ Principles

attributes.name: reference_period_start

attributes.description: Reference to the investigational site at which the anomaly or Key Risk Indicator (KRI) threshold breach was detected. Core contextual dimension for risk-based monitoring (RBM) triage.

attributes.name: alert_category
attributes.description: Broad business domain category of the alert, used for routing, reporting, and escalation prioritization. DATA_QUALITY: data entry or consistency issues. SAFETY: adverse event or safety reporting concerns.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; CDISC RBM Reference Model

attributes.name: alert_generated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the alert was generated by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system or manually created by a central monitor. This is the principal real-world business event time. BUSINESS_EVENT_TIMESTAMP category.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: alert_number
attributes.description: Human-readable, externally-known business identifier for the alert, formatted as CMA-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in communications, reports, and audit trails to uniquely reference an alert across systems. Sourced from the source system
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; CDISC RBM Reference Model

attributes.name: alert_severity
attributes.description: Risk-stratified severity level of the alert, driving escalation urgency and response timelines. CRITICAL: immediate action required, potential patient safety or data integrity risk. HIGH: significant risk requiring prompt review within defined SLA.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: alert_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle state of the alert within the review and disposition workflow. OPEN: generated and awaiting assignment. UNDER_REVIEW: assigned reviewer is actively assessing. ESCALATED: elevated to on-site visit or senior oversight.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: alert_type
attributes.description: Classification of the alert by the nature of the triggering condition. KRI_THRESHOLD_BREACH: a Key Risk Indicator exceeded its amber or red threshold. DATA_ANOMALY: a data pattern inconsistency detected by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM)
attributes.references: TransCelerate RBM Initiative; CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: assignment_date
attributes.description: Date on which the alert was assigned to a reviewer for investigation. Used to measure assignment SLA compliance from alert generation to assignment.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: capa_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether a Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) must be initiated as a result of this alert. Set to True when disposition is CAPA_INITIATED or when a confirmed critical finding requires systematic remediation.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); MasterControl CAPA; FDA 21 CFR Part 820; ISO 14155

tag_set.value: Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) Required Flag

attributes.name: consecutive_breach_count
attributes.description: Number of consecutive computation cycles in which the triggering KRI has breached its threshold at this site prior to and including this alert. A higher count indicates a persistent risk pattern and informs escalation urgency.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this alert record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Distinct from alert_generated_timestamp which captures the business event time. RECORD_AUDIT_CREATED category.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: disposition
attributes.description: Action decision made following review of the alert. ESCALATE_ONSITE_VISIT: alert severity warrants an unscheduled or triggered on-site monitoring visit. REMOTE_FOLLOW_UP: issue to be addressed via remote monitoring or site communication.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: escalation_date
attributes.description: Date on which the alert was formally escalated to a higher oversight level. Null when escalation_required is False. Used to track escalation timeliness and compliance with monitoring plan escalation SLAs.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: escalation_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alert has been escalated to a higher level of oversight (e.g., sponsor, Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB), or senior management). True when disposition is ESCALATE_ONSITE_VISIT or when severity is CRITICAL.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: is_repeat_alert
attributes.description: Indicates whether this alert is a recurrence of a previously closed alert for the same KRI and site within the current study. True when a prior alert for the same KRI-site combination was closed and the KRI has breached again, signaling unresolved
attributes.references: TransCelerate RBM Initiative; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: kri_code
attributes.description: Key risk indicator code. Implements ICH E6(R2) GCP 5.0 risk-based monitoring KRI concept.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: kri_name
attributes.description: Human-readable name of the Key Risk Indicator (KRI) that triggered the alert (e.g., 'Adverse Event Reporting Timeliness', 'Query Resolution Rate'). Denormalized for alert reporting and dashboard display without requiring a join to the risk_indicator
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: observed_value
attributes.description: The actual computed value of the Key Risk Indicator (KRI) or data signal at the time the alert was generated. Compared against threshold_value to confirm the breach. QUANTITATIVE_RESULT category per TRANSACTION_HEADER non-monetary role.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: reference_period_end
attributes.description: End date of the data analysis window used by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system to compute the KRI value that triggered this alert. Together with reference_period_start, defines the exact data window under review.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: reference_period_start
attributes.description: Start date of the data analysis window used by the centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) system to compute the KRI value that triggered this alert. Defines the temporal scope of the anomaly.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: review_completed_date
attributes.description: Actual date on which the reviewer completed the assessment and recorded a disposition for the alert. Used to calculate review cycle time and SLA compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: review_due_date
attributes.description: Target date by which the assigned reviewer must complete the review and disposition of the alert, as defined by the monitoring plan SLA for the given alert severity level.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); Oracle Siebel CTMS; TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: review_narrative
attributes.description: Free-text narrative entered by the reviewer documenting the findings, rationale for the review outcome, and justification for the chosen disposition. Supports audit trail and regulatory inspection readiness per ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+ Principles; 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: review_outcome
attributes.description: Conclusion reached by the reviewer after investigating the alert. CONFIRMED: the anomaly or KRI breach is genuine and requires action. FALSE_POSITIVE: the alert was triggered in error or the signal is not clinically meaningful.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate RBM Initiative; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: source_system_record_reference
attributes.description: Native record identifier from the originating operational system (the source system or CSM engine) for this alert. Enables lineage tracing and reconciliation between the Silver Layer and the system of record.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: sponsor_notification_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sponsor was formally notified of this alert. Null when sponsor_notified is False. Used to verify compliance with sponsor notification SLAs defined in the monitoring plan.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; Oracle Siebel CTMS

attributes.name: sponsor_notified
attributes.description: Indicates whether the study sponsor has been formally notified of this alert, as required for critical or high-severity alerts under the monitoring plan and sponsor oversight obligations per ICH E6(R2).
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) Section 5.18; FDA Guidance on Risk-Based Monitoring

attributes.name: threshold_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the breached threshold was the amber (warning) or red (action-required) threshold level as defined in the monitoring plan. Drives escalation logic and response SLA.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; TransCelerate RBM Initiative; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: threshold_value
attributes.description: The amber or red threshold value that was breached at the time the alert was generated. Captured at alert generation time to preserve the threshold configuration in effect, as thresholds may be revised over the study lifecycle.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; ICH E6(R2); TransCelerate RBM Initiative

attributes.name: trigger_source
attributes.description: System or process that generated the alert. AUTOMATED_CSM: centralized statistical monitoring (CSM) engine. MANUAL_ENTRY: entered directly by a central monitor.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; Oracle Siebel CTMS; Medidata Rave

attributes.name: unit_of_measure
attributes.description: Unit in which the observed_value and threshold_value are expressed (e.g., 'percent', 'days', 'count', 'ratio'). Required for correct interpretation of the KRI metric values in alert review and reporting.
attributes.references: CDISC RBM Reference Model; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this alert record was last modified in the Databricks Silver Layer, capturing status changes, review updates, and disposition entries. RECORD_AUDIT_UPDATED category.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ Principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: analysis_phase
attributes.description: Designates the analysis phase in which this population definition is applied: interim analysis, final analysis, post-hoc analysis, or exploratory analysis. Governs which TLF shells and CSR sections reference this population.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E3; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: blinding_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the analysis population is evaluated under blinded, unblinded, or open-label conditions at the time of analysis. Critical for DSMB/DMC interim reviews and final unblinding records.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 5.5; ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on Blinding

attributes.name: cdisc_standard_version
attributes.business_glossary_term: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Standard Version
attributes.description: The version of the CDISC ADaM standard applied to the derivation of this analysis population (e.g., ADaM IG v1.3, ADSL v1.1). Required for FDA/EMA electronic submission conformance.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; EMA Data Standards

tag_set.value: Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Standard Version

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this analysis population record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: dbl_date
attributes.description: The date on which the study database was locked (DBL) for the analysis associated with this population. Subject counts and population assignments are finalized as of this date.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Guidance on DBL; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: dose_received_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether receipt of at least one dose of investigational product is a mandatory inclusion criterion for this analysis population. Distinguishes ITT (randomized only) from Safety (randomized and dosed) populations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on Safety Populations

attributes.name: effective_from_date
attributes.description: The date from which this version of the analysis population definition became effective, supporting the source system Enables temporal tracking of population definition changes across the source system
attributes.references: ICH E9; Veeva Vault eTMF; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: exclusion_criteria_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the criteria that would exclude a subject from this analysis population despite meeting inclusion criteria (e.g., major protocol deviations, missing primary endpoint data). Defined in the the source system.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; ICH E3

attributes.name: inclusion_criteria_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the criteria a subject must meet to be included in this analysis population, as defined in the the source system. Captures the logical rules (e.g., randomized and received at least one dose of study drug).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: missing_endpoint_handling
attributes.description: The pre-specified method for handling missing primary endpoint data for subjects in this population, as defined in the the source system - Last Observation Carried Forward, multiple imputation, observed cases only).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.4; FDA Guidance on Missing Data; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for biostatistician notes, clarifications, or amendments related to this analysis population definition. May capture DSMB/DMC recommendations, protocol amendment impacts, or sponsor queries.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: planned_sample_size
attributes.description: The pre-specified planned number of subjects for this analysis population as determined by the sample size calculation in the the source system. Serves as the denominator benchmark for enrollment tracking and power calculations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.5; FDA Guidance on Sample Size; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: population_code
attributes.description: Short, unique alphanumeric code identifying the analysis population within the study (e.g., ITT, PP, SAF, MITT, PK). Used as the CDISC ADaM ADSL flag variable name prefix and in TLF shell headers.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide v1.3; CDISC ADSL

attributes.name: population_finalized_date
attributes.description: The date on which the analysis population definition was formally finalized and approved in the the source system, prior to unblinding. Supports pre-specification audit trail for regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2); 21 CFR Part 11; FDA Guidance on Pre-specification

attributes.name: population_logic_summary
attributes.description: Concise programmatic or pseudo-code summary of the population derivation logic used in SAS Drug Development ADaM programming (e.g., RANDFL='Y' AND DOSEFL='Y'). Bridges the narrative the source system the SAS implementation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; SAS Drug Development Best Practices

attributes.name: population_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the analysis population as defined in the the source system Population, Per Protocol Population, Safety Population, Modified Intent-to-Treat Population, Pharmacokinetic Population).
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: population_rationale
attributes.description: Scientific and regulatory rationale for defining this analysis population, as documented in the the source system. Explains why this population is appropriate for the associated analysis objectives and how it aligns with regulatory guidance.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E3 Section 9.7; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: population_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the analysis population definition. Tracks progression from initial the source system biostatistics review, approval, and potential supersession by an amended the source system
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; GCP ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: population_type
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the analysis population by its primary analytical purpose. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: efficacy|safety|pharmacokinetic|pharmacodynamic|per_protocol|modified_itt|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM Implementation Guide

attributes.name: primary_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is designated as the primary analysis population for the study as specified in the the source system. The primary population drives the primary efficacy endpoint analysis and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.2; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: protocol_deviation_exclusion_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether subjects with major protocol deviations are excluded from this analysis population. Typically True for Per Protocol (PP) populations and False for ITT populations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2); CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: randomization_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether randomization is a mandatory inclusion criterion for subjects in this analysis population. True for ITT and most efficacy populations; may be False for screening failure or safety populations.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on ITT Principle

attributes.name: regulatory_primary_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is the pre-specified primary population for regulatory submission purposes (NDA/BLA/MAA). Distinct from internal primary flag; reflects the population declared in the IND/protocol.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA Guideline on Clinical Trials; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: sap_section_reference
attributes.description: The specific section number or identifier within the the source system formally defines this analysis population (e.g., Section 5.2.1). Enables direct traceability from the data product to the governing statistical document.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E3; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: sap_version
attributes.description: Version number of the the source system which this analysis population definition was introduced or last amended (e.g., v1.0, v2.1). Supports version-controlled traceability for regulatory audit.
attributes.references: ICH E9; Veeva Vault eTMF versioning; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: sas_program_name
attributes.description: Name of the SAS Drug Development program used to derive and validate the ADSL flag variable for this analysis population (e.g., adsl.sas). Enables traceability from population definition to the validated SAS code.
attributes.references: SAS Drug Development; CDISC ADaM; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide

attributes.name: sensitivity_analysis_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this population is designated as a sensitivity analysis population (as opposed to a primary or secondary analysis population). Sensitivity populations test the robustness of primary analysis conclusions.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 3.8; FDA Guidance on Sensitivity Analyses

attributes.name: subject_count_at_dbl
attributes.description: The number of subjects assigned to this analysis population at the time of Database Lock (DBL). This is the final, locked count used in the Clinical Study Report (CSR) and regulatory submission.
attributes.references: ICH E3 Section 10.1; CDISC ADaM; FDA Guidance on DBL

attributes.name: subject_count_interim
attributes.description: Number of subjects assigned to this analysis population at the most recent interim analysis cut, if applicable. Used by the DSMB/DMC for interim review and blinded/unblinded reporting.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1) Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs; DSMB Charter

attributes.name: submission_population_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this analysis population is included in the regulatory submission package (NDA/BLA/MAA/eCTD). Populations marked True must have fully validated ADaM datasets and TLF outputs.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 314; EMA EU CTR 536/2014; ICH M4E (CTD Module 5)

attributes.name: tlf_shell_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) Shell Reference
attributes.description: Reference identifier(s) for the TLF shells that use this analysis population as their denominator or subject set. Links the population definition to the output specifications in the the source system/TLF shell document.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; ICH E3; SAS Drug Development TLF Specifications

tag_set.value: Tables, Listings, and Figures (TLF) Shell Reference

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this analysis population record was last modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11 and ALCOA+ principles.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2); ALCOA+; GDPR Article 5

attributes.name: validation_status
attributes.description: Current validation status of the SAS programming for this analysis population's ADSL flag variable in SAS Drug Development. Tracks QC progress from initial programming through double-programming validation.
attributes.references: CDISC ADaM; FDA Study Data Technical Conformance Guide; GCP ICH E6(R2)

products.name: sample_size_calc
products.description: Records sample size calculations performed during study design and protocol development. Captures study phase, primary endpoint type, assumed effect size, standard deviation, alpha level, power, dropout rate, allocation ratio, calculated sample size per
products.reference: Sample Size Calculation — ICH E9, FDA Guidance on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: sample_size_calc_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sample size calculation record within the biostatistics domain.
attributes.references: ICH E9 Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials

attributes.name: analysis_population_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to biostatistics.analysis_population. Business justification: sample_size_calc has analysis_population (STRING) indicating which population the sample size calculation targets.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: approved_by_employee_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Sample size calculations require a named approving statistician for protocol and regulatory submission documentation.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: pipeline_asset_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to sponsor.pipeline_asset. Business justification: Sample size assumptions (effect_size, dropout_rate, event_rate_control) are derived from the pipeline asset's prior clinical data and development phase.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: protocol_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific protocol version under which this sample size calculation was conducted, supporting traceability to protocol amendments.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: rand_scheme_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to randomization.rand_scheme. Business justification: Sample size calculations depend directly on the randomization scheme's allocation_ratio, block structure, and stratification.
attributes.references: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

attributes.name: sap_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Statistical Analysis Plan (the source system) document that governs or references this sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1) Addendum on Estimands

attributes.name: study_id
attributes.description: Reference to the clinical study for which this sample size calculation was performed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM

attributes.name: accrual_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed patient accrual (enrollment) period in months, used in time-to-event sample size calculations to determine the number of events required.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: allocation_ratio
attributes.description: The randomization allocation ratio between treatment arms (e.g., '1:1', '2:1', '1:1:1'), specifying the relative number of subjects assigned to each arm.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Randomization Standards

attributes.name: alpha_level
attributes.description: The pre-specified Type I error rate (significance level, alpha) used in the sample size calculation, typically 0.05 for two-sided or 0.025 for one-sided tests.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; EMA Guideline on Multiplicity

attributes.name: alpha_spending_method
attributes.description: The alpha-spending function applied to control Type I error across planned interim analyses (e.g., O'Brien-Fleming, Pocock, Lan-DeMets). Null or 'none' if no interim analysis is planned.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: amendment_reason
attributes.description: Narrative justification for revising a prior version of the sample size calculation, such as updated assumptions from interim data, protocol amendment, or regulatory feedback.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Protocol Amendment Guidance; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the sample size calculation was formally approved by the responsible biostatistician, marking readiness for inclusion in regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_date
attributes.description: The date on which this sample size calculation was performed or finalized, serving as the principal business event date for regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: calc_identifier
attributes.description: Externally-known alphanumeric code or reference number assigned to this sample size calculation, used in regulatory submissions and protocol documentation (e.g., SSC-2024-001).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: calc_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sample size calculation record, from initial draft through regulatory approval to archival.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: calc_version
attributes.description: Version number of this sample size calculation (e.g., v1.0, v2.1), enabling tracking of revisions driven by protocol amendments or updated assumptions.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail requirements under 21 CFR Part 11.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.name: dropout_rate
attributes.description: The assumed proportion of enrolled subjects expected to discontinue or be lost to follow-up, used to inflate the calculated sample size to ensure adequate evaluable subjects.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Missing Data in Clinical Trials

attributes.name: effect_size
attributes.description: The clinically meaningful difference or effect size assumed between treatment arms (e.g., mean difference, odds ratio, hazard ratio) used as the basis for the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Guidance on Sample Size Calculations

attributes.name: effect_size_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measurement for the assumed effect size (e.g., mmHg, %, hazard ratio, odds ratio, mean difference), providing dimensional context for regulatory interpretation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; CDISC SDTM Unit Standards

attributes.name: event_rate_control
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the control arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: event_rate_treatment
attributes.description: The assumed event rate or response rate in the treatment arm, applicable for binary or time-to-event endpoints. Null for continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: follow_up_period_months
attributes.description: The assumed minimum follow-up period in months after the last patient enrolled, used in time-to-event calculations to ensure sufficient events are observed.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: hypothesis_type
attributes.description: The statistical hypothesis framework applied (superiority, non-inferiority, equivalence), which determines the directionality and margin used in the sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10 Choice of Control Group; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance

attributes.name: interim_analysis_planned
attributes.description: Indicates whether one or more interim analyses are planned for this study, which may require alpha-spending adjustments to the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: median_survival_control
attributes.description: The assumed median survival time in the control arm for time-to-event endpoints, used in log-rank or exponential model-based sample size calculations. Null for non-survival endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance

attributes.name: non_inferiority_margin
attributes.description: The pre-specified non-inferiority or equivalence margin (delta) used in the hypothesis test, applicable when hypothesis_type is non_inferiority or equivalence. Null for superiority designs.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10; FDA Non-Inferiority Guidance 2016

attributes.name: number_of_arms
attributes.description: Total number of treatment arms (including control) in the study design, used to determine the allocation structure and multiplicity adjustments.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E10

attributes.name: number_of_events_required
attributes.description: The minimum number of primary endpoint events (e.g., deaths, progressions) required to achieve the specified power for time-to-event analyses. Null for non-event-driven endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Oncology Endpoint Guidance; EMA Guideline on Survival Analysis

attributes.name: power
attributes.description: The pre-specified statistical power (1 minus Type II error rate, beta) used in the calculation, representing the probability of detecting the assumed effect size. Typically 0.80 or 0.90.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the primary endpoint used in the sample size calculation (e.g., 'Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24'), providing clinical context for regulatory reviewers.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); FDA Guidance on Clinical Trial Endpoints

attributes.name: primary_endpoint_type
attributes.description: Statistical nature of the primary efficacy endpoint (e.g., continuous, binary, time-to-event, ordinal, count) that drives the choice of sample size formula.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1) Estimands Addendum; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: reference_source
attributes.description: Citation or reference for the data source used to derive the assumed effect size, standard deviation, or event rate (e.g., published literature citation, prior Phase II study identifier, internal pilot data).
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: sample_size_per_arm
attributes.description: The calculated number of subjects required per treatment arm to achieve the specified power at the given alpha level, accounting for the assumed effect size and standard deviation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: software_name
attributes.description: Name of the validated statistical software used to perform the sample size calculation (e.g., PASS, nQuery Advisor, SAS PROC POWER, R), required for regulatory audit trail.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; CDISC Validation Standards

attributes.name: software_version
attributes.description: Version number of the statistical software used (e.g., PASS 2023, nQuery 9.1), required for reproducibility and regulatory validation documentation.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E9; 21 CFR Part 820 (software validation)

attributes.name: standard_deviation
attributes.description: The assumed population standard deviation for continuous endpoints, derived from prior studies or literature, used in the sample size formula. Null for non-continuous endpoints.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: statistical_method
attributes.description: The specific statistical formula or method used for the calculation (e.g., two-sample t-test, log-rank test, chi-square test, Kaplan-Meier), providing methodological traceability.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance; CDISC ADaM

attributes.name: study_design_type
attributes.description: The clinical trial design type (e.g., parallel group, crossover, factorial, adaptive) that determines the statistical methodology applied in the sample size calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9; ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance

attributes.name: study_phase
attributes.description: Clinical development phase of the study (Phase I through Phase IV) for which the sample size is being calculated, influencing regulatory expectations and statistical rigor.
attributes.value_regex: Phase I|Phase II|Phase IIa|Phase IIb|Phase III|Phase IV
attributes.references: ICH E8 General Considerations for Clinical Trials; FDA 21 CFR Part 312

attributes.name: test_sidedness
attributes.description: Specifies whether the statistical test is one-sided or two-sided, directly affecting the critical value and resulting sample size.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: total_enrollment_target
attributes.description: The total number of subjects to be enrolled (randomized) after inflating the total sample size by the assumed dropout rate, representing the actual recruitment target submitted in the protocol.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA 21 CFR Part 312; EU CTR 536/2014

attributes.name: total_sample_size
attributes.description: The total number of subjects required across all treatment arms before applying the dropout inflation, representing the minimum evaluable sample.
attributes.references: ICH E9; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this sample size calculation record was most recently modified, supporting version control and audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: FDA 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles; ICH E6(R2)

attributes.description: Total number of primary endpoint events required for the final analysis as specified in the the source system size calculation. Used as the denominator for the information fraction in event-driven trials.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: firewall_maintained
attributes.description: Indicates whether a blinding firewall was maintained between the unblinded interim analysis team and the blinded study team (True = firewall in place; False = firewall not maintained or not applicable).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: futility_boundary_binding
attributes.description: Indicates whether the futility stopping boundary is binding (True = mandatory stop if crossed; False = non-binding/advisory only). Binding futility boundaries affect the overall Type I error calculation.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: futility_boundary_value
attributes.description: Pre-specified critical value for the futility stopping boundary at this interim look. If the observed test statistic falls below this boundary, early stopping for futility (lack of efficacy) may be triggered.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; EMA Reflection Paper on Adaptive Designs

attributes.name: information_fraction_actual
attributes.description: Observed proportion of total planned statistical information actually accumulated at the time of this interim analysis. May differ from planned fraction due to enrollment variability or event rate changes.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Lan-DeMets alpha spending framework

attributes.name: information_fraction_planned
attributes.description: Pre-specified proportion of the total planned statistical information (e.g., events, subjects) accumulated at the time of this interim analysis, expressed as a decimal between 0 and 1 (e.g., 0.5000 = 50% of planned events).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); Lan-DeMets alpha spending framework; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for capturing additional context, operational notes, deviations from the pre-specified plan, or DSMB/DMC commentary relevant to this interim analysis that is not captured in structured fields.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: observed_p_value
attributes.description: The nominal p-value from the primary hypothesis test at this interim analysis. Must be interpreted in the context of the alpha spending boundary, not as a standalone significance threshold.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; FDA Statistical Guidance

attributes.name: observed_test_statistic
attributes.description: The actual computed test statistic (e.g., z-score, chi-square, log-rank statistic) from the interim analysis dataset. Compared against efficacy and futility boundaries to determine the outcome.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC ADaM; SAS Drug Development

attributes.name: planned_analysis_date
attributes.description: Pre-specified calendar date on which the interim analysis is planned to be conducted, as documented in the the source system charter.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) GCP

attributes.name: regulatory_submission_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interim analysis results or the resulting design adaptation must be submitted to a regulatory authority (FDA, EMA, PMDA, etc.) as part of an IND, NDA, BLA, or MAA amendment (True = submission required; False = not required).
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 312; FDA IND Regulations; EMA Clinical Trial Regulation EU CTR 536/2014; ICH E9(R1)

attributes.name: results_disclosed_externally
attributes.description: Indicates whether the interim analysis results have been disclosed externally (e.g., to regulators, in a public registry, or in a publication) prior to study completion (True = disclosed; False = not disclosed).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); WHO ICTRP; EU CTR 536/2014; FDA Transparency Guidance

attributes.name: revised_sample_size
attributes.description: Updated total sample size determined through the pre-specified sample size re-estimation procedure at this interim analysis. Null if sample_size_reestimated is False.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: sample_size_reestimated
attributes.description: Indicates whether a pre-specified sample size re-estimation was performed as part of this interim analysis (True = sample size re-estimated; False = no re-estimation performed).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: sas_program_version
attributes.description: Version identifier of the SAS Drug Development program or analysis package used to execute this interim analysis, enabling reproducibility and audit traceability.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; CDISC ADaM; SAS Drug Development platform

attributes.name: stopping_rule_description
attributes.description: Narrative description of the specific stopping rule(s) triggered at this interim analysis, including the criterion crossed and the observed vs. boundary values. Populated only when stopping_rule_triggered is True.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: stopping_rule_triggered
attributes.description: Indicates whether any pre-specified stopping rule (efficacy, futility, or safety) was triggered by the results of this interim analysis (True = stopping rule crossed; False = no stopping rule triggered).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019

attributes.name: subjects_enrolled_at_cutoff
attributes.description: Total number of subjects enrolled in the study as of the data cutoff date for this interim analysis. Provides context for the information fraction and statistical power.
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); CDISC SDTM DM domain

attributes.name: unblinding_authorization_date
attributes.description: Date on which formal authorization was granted to unblind the interim analysis data, as documented in the unblinding log. Required for audit trail and blinding integrity compliance.
attributes.references: ICH E6(R2) GCP; 21 CFR Part 11; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: unblinding_scope
attributes.description: Defines the extent of treatment assignment unblinding performed for this interim analysis: full (all treatment assignments revealed to the analysis team), partial (only aggregate or summary-level unblinding), or none (blinded analysis only).
attributes.references: ICH E9(R1); ICH E6(R2) GCP; FDA Adaptive Design Guidance 2019; 21 CFR Part 11

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this interim analysis record was most recently modified, supporting audit trail requirements and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
attributes.references: 21 CFR Part 11; ICH E6(R2) GCP; ALCOA+ principles

attributes.name: dbl_event_number

attributes.name: dm_approval_timestamp

attributes.name: lock_scope

attributes.name: lock_timestamp

attributes.name: outstanding_query_count
